questions.q: At $298K$, the equilibrium constant of the process $1 . 5{O}_{2 ( g )} ⇌ {O}_{3 ( g )}$ is $3 \times {10}^{- 29}$. Standard free energy change (in $kJ{mol}^{- 1}$ ) of the process is approximately  \left(R = 8 . 314J{mol}^{- 1}K^{- 1}; log3 = 0 . 47\right)$
questions.solution:
Free energy change of a reaction is calculated by,

$∆ G = ∆ G^{∘} + RTlnQ$

At equilibrium, the free energy change of a reaction~is zero $( ∆ G = 0 )$, and the reaction quotient~$( Q )$~is equal to the equilibrium constant~$( K )$. So, the above relation takes the form,

$∆ G^{∘} = - RTlnK$

$∆ G^{∘} = - 2 . 303RT\log_{10}K$

where~$∆ G^{∘} =$standard free energy change

Therefore,

$∆ G^{∘} = - 2 . 303 \times 8 . 314 \times 298 \times log\left(3 \times {10}^{- 29}\right)J{mol}^{- 1}$

$∆ G^{∘} = - 5705 . 8 \times \left[log\left(3\right) + log\left({10}^{- 29}\right)\right]J{mol}^{- 1}$

$∆ G^{∘} = - 5705 . 8 \times \left[0 . 47 - 29\right]J{mol}^{- 1}$

$∆ G^{∘} = 162787J{mol}^{- 1}$

$∆ G^{∘} \approx 163kJ{mol}^{- 1}$

questions.q: If $92gNa$~reacts with water in open vessel at $300K$. What is the value of work done? [Assume ideal nature of the gaseous product]
questions.solution:
Reaction of sodium with water will be&

$2{Na}_{( s )} + 2{H}_{2}{O}_{( l )} \to 2{NaOH}_{( aq )} + {H}_{2 ( g )}$

According to the given reaction 46 g of Na gives one mole of hydrogen gas.

So, 92 g of Na will give~$= \dfrac{92}{46} = 2molesof{H}_{2}gas$

This is the only gaseous product so, due to this volume will increase at constant pressure.

Work done at constant pressure and temperature

$w = - P ∆ V = - ∆ {n}_{g}RT$~ since product is ideal gas.

$w = - 2 \times 8 . 314 \times 300J = - 4988 . 4J$

Negative sign indicate that work is done by the system.

questions.q: What is the standard enthalpy of reaction (in kJ) when two moles of $\mathrm{Fe}_2 \mathrm{O}_3(s)$ reacts with $\mathrm{H}_2$ gas to give Fe metal? $\Delta H_f^{{}^{{}^{\circ}}}$ of $\mathrm{Fe}_2 \mathrm{O}_3(s)$ and $\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}(l)$ are -824.2 and $-285.83 \mathrm{~kJ} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1}$ respectively.
questions.solution: When $\mathrm{Fe}_2 \mathrm{O}_3(s)$ reacts with $\mathrm{H}_2(g)$, it will give $\mathrm{Fe}$ and $\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}$ as follows: $\mathrm{Fe}_2 \mathrm{O}_3+3 \mathrm{H}_2 \rightarrow 2 \mathrm{Fe}+3 \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}$ When 2 moles of $\mathrm{Fe}_2 \mathrm{O}_3$ are used, the reaction becomes as follows: $2  \left[\mathrm{Fe}_2 \mathrm{O}_3+3 \mathrm{H}_2 \rightarrow 2 \mathrm{Fe}+3 \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}\right]$ Given, $\Delta H_f^{\circ}$ for $\mathrm{Fe}_2 \mathrm{O}_3(s)=-824.2 \mathrm{~kJ} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1}$ and $\Delta H_f^{\circ}$ for $\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}(l)=-285.83 \mathrm{~kJ} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1}\because$ Standard enthalpy of reaction \left(\Delta H_R^{\circ}\$right)=\sum \Delta$H_f^{\circ}$ (Product) $-\Sigma \Delta H_f^{\circ}$ (Reacant $)$ and \left.$\begin{array}{c}$H_f^{\circ} \text { for } \mathrm{H}_2=0 \\ H_f^{\circ} \text { for } \mathrm{Fe}=0\end{array}\right]$ (as are present in free state) Thus, \begin{aligned} \Delta$H_R^{\circ} & =[6 \times-285.83]-[2 \times(-824.2)] \\ \Delta H_R^{\circ} & =(-1714.98)+(1648.4) \\ \Delta H_R^{\circ} & =-66.58 \mathrm{~kJ} / \mathrm{mol}\end{aligned}$ Hence, option (a) is the correct answer.$

questions.q: Consider the reversible isothermal expansion of an ideal gas in a closed system at two different temperatures ${T}_{1}$ and ${T}_{2}  \left({T}_{1}< {T}_{2}\right) .$~The correct graphical depiction of the dependence of work done~\left(w\right)$ on the final volume~\left(v\right) .$
questions.solution:
Let the gas is expanded from ${V}_{1}$ to $V$ at ${T}_{1}$ and from ${V}_{2}$ to $V$at ${T}_{2}$

$∴$ At ${T}_{1}$

\left|{W}_{1}\right| = nR{T}_{1}ln\dfrac{V}{V1} = nRT\left(ℓnV - ℓ{nV}_{1}\right)$

Similarly at~${T}_{2}$

\left|{W}_{2}\right| = nR{T}_{2} \left(lnV - ln{V}_{2} )\right$

$∴ {W}_{1} = {nRT}_{1}lnV - {nRT}_{1}{lnV}_{1}$

${W}_{2} = {nRT}_{2}lnV - {nRT}_{2}{lnV}_{2}$

Slope of~${W}_{2} >$Slope of~${W}_{1}$

As~$nR{T}_{2} > nR{T}_{1} \left({T}_{2}> {T}_{1}\right)$

$∴$ The intercept of ${W}_{2}$ is more negative than that of ${W}_{1}$ because ${V}_{2} > {V}_{1} .

$

questions.solution: Weight of graphite \(=6 $\mathrm{~g}$\) In bomb calorimeter volume is constant Hence, \(W=0\), (work done) \(\Delta H=\Delta U=q $\text { (Heat) }$\) Given, \(\Delta H=-248 $\mathrm{~kJ}$/ $\mathrm{mol}$\) For, \(12 $\mathrm{~g}$\) of graphite required energy is \(248 $\mathrm{~kJ}$/ $\mathrm{mol}$\). questions.q: The change in the internal energy when a system goes from state& $AtoBis40kJ{mole}^{- 1}$.~If the system follows a reversible path from~$A$ to $B$~and returns to state $A$ by an irreversible path, what would be the net change in internal energy?
questions.solution:
We know that, internal energy is a state function, hence it only depends upon the initial and final values irrespective of the path followed,

i.e.,& $∆ U = {U}_{final} - {U}_{initial}$

For the given cyclic process:

${U}_{final} = {U}_{initial}$

Thus, the net change in internal energy change is zero.

questions.q: Standard entropies of ${X}_{2}, {Y}_{2}$~and ${XY}_{3}$ are $60, 40$ and $50J / K / mol$ respectively. At what temperature the following reaction will be at equilibrium
questions.solution:
So from this question we know that enthalpy for the reaction is& $- 30KJ$

$\dfrac{1}{2}{X}_{2} + \dfrac{3}{2}{Y}_{2} \to {XY}_{3}$~ ~ ~ & & & $∆ H = - 30KJ$

So we know from the concept of standard entropies is~

$∆ S = ∆ S\left(P\right) - ∆ S\left(R\right) ∆ S = ∆ S\left({XY}_{3}\right) - \dfrac{3}{2} ∆ S\left({Y}_{2}\right) - \dfrac{1}{2} ∆ S\left({X}_{2}\right) ∆ S = 50 - \dfrac{3}{2} \times 40 - \dfrac{1}{2} \times 60 ∆ S = - 40{JK}^{- 1}{mol}^{- 1}$

So according to the second law of thermodynamics

$∆ G = ∆ H - T ∆ S$

For equilibrium the free Gibb's energy is~$∆ G = 0$

$∆ H = T ∆ ST = \dfrac{∆ H}{∆ S}T = \dfrac{- 30 \times {10}^{3}J}{- 40{JK}^{- 1}}$

So the value of temperature is~

$T = 750K$

questions.q: At $60 ° C$, dinitrogen tetroxide is fifty percent dissociated. Find its standard free energy change at this temperature and one atmosphere. [ Given: $log1 . 33 = 0 . 1239$& ]
questions.solution:
The reaction showing the dissociation will be:

$\begin{cases} & {N}_{2}{O}_{4} ( s ) & ⇌ & 2{NO}_{2} ( g ) \\ t = 0 & 1mol & & 0mol \\ t = {t}_{eq} & 0 . 5mol & & 1mol\end{cases}$

Clearly,~from this equation we can say that the total number of moles is~

$0 . 5 + 1 = 1 . 5mol$

Hence, the partial pressure for the molecule will be

${P}_{{N}_{2}{O}_{4}} = \dfrac{0 . 5}{1 . 5} \times 1atm = \dfrac{1}{3}atm{P}_{NO2} = \dfrac{1}{1 . 5} \times 1atm = \dfrac{2}{3}atm$

Now, according to the law of chemical equilibrium we know that~

${K}_{sp} = \dfrac{P^{2}{NO}_{2}}{P{N}_{2}{O}_{4}} = \dfrac{\left(\dfrac{2}{3}\right)2}{\dfrac{1}{3}} = 1 . 33atm$

We know that at equilibrium the free Gibb's energy is:~

$∆ G = - 2 . 303 \times RT \times \left(\log_{10}{K}_{P}\right) ∆ G = - 2 . 303 \times \left(8 . 314{JK}^{- 1}{mol}^{- 1}\right) \times \left(333K\right) \times \left[\log_{10}\left(1 . 33\right)\right] ∆ G = - 790{Jmol}^{- 1}$

questions.q: What is the amount of work done when 0.5 mole of methane, $C{H}_{4}  \left(g\right)$~is subjected to combustion at 300 K? (Given, $R = 8.314JK^{- 1}mol^{- 1} )$
questions.solution:
$C{H}_{4} ( g ) + 2{O}_{2} ( g ) \to C{O}_{2} ( g ) + 2{H}_{2} O( l )$
Amount of work done~$= - ∆ nRT$
1 mole of methane reacts with 2 moles of oxygen to produce 2 moles of $C{O}_{2}$
Hence, 0.5 mole of $C{H}_{4}$ reacts with 1 mole of ${O}_{2}$ to produce 1 mole of $C{O}_{2}$.
$∴ {n}_{1} =$ moles of reactants = 1.5
${n}_{2} =$ moles of product = 1
$∴ ∆ n = {n}_{2} - {n}_{1} = 1 - 1.5 = - 0.5$
$w = - \left(- 0.5\right) \times 300 \times 8.314JK^{- 1}mol^{- 1}$
$= + 2494J$

questions.q:
A thermodynamic& cycle in the& pressure \left(P\right)$-volume \left(V\right)$ plane is given below:

$AB$ and $CD$ are isothermal processes while $BC$ and $DA$ are adiabatic processes. The same cycle in the temperature \left(T\right)$- entropy \left(S\right)$ plane is :
questions.solution:
$AB$ is isothermal reversible expansion process i.e. $\Delta T = 0$~and $S$ increases as there is increase in volume.

$BC$~is adiabatic reversible expansion process~ \left({q}_{rev} = 0\right)$~i.e. temperature decreases and $\Delta S = 0$

$CD$ is isothermal reversible compression process i.e. $\Delta T = 0$~and $S$ decreases as there is decrease in volume.

$DA$ is adiabatic reversible compression process \left({q}_{res} = 0\right)$~i.e. temperature decreases and $\Delta S = 0$

questions.solution:
Temperature at& $A\left({T}_{A}\right) = \dfrac{P{V}_{0}}{nR}$

${T}_{B} = \dfrac{2{P}_{0}{V}_{0}}{nR}$

Since $BC$ curve isothermal

${T}_{D} = \dfrac{\left({P}_{0} / 2\right) \cdot 2{V}_{0}}{nR} = \dfrac{{P}_{0}{V}_{0}}{nR} = {T}_{A}$

Now

$∵ {T}_{D} - {T}_{A} = 0$

$∴ \Delta U = \Delta H = 0$

\left\{∵ Foridealgas\begin{array}{ll}\Delta U = {nC}_{V}\Delta T \\ \Delta H = {nC}_{P}\Delta T\end{array}\right\}$

${W}_{T} = {W}_{AB} + {W}_{BC} + {W}_{CD}$

$= - {P}_{0}{V}_{0} + - nRTln\dfrac{4{V}_{0}}{2{V}_{0}} + \left(- $\dfrac{P0}{2} \times -$2{V}_{0}\right)$

${W}_{τ} = - 2{P}_{0}{V}_{0}ln2$~and~$q = - {W}_{T}$

$

questions.q:
Given:

$\text{C}\left(\text{graphite}\right) + {O}_{2} \left(\text{g}\right) \to {\text{CO}}_{2} \left(\text{g}\right); {Δ}_{r} H^{o} = - 393.5{\text{kJ mol}}^{- 1}$

${\text{H}}_{2}\left(\text{g}\right) + \dfrac{1}{2}{\text{O}}_{2}\left(\text{g}\right) \to {\text{H}}_{2}\text{O}\left(\text{l}\right); {\text{\Delta}}_{\text{r}}{\text{H}}^{\text{o}} = - 285.8\text{k}\text{J}\text{m}\text{o}{\text{l}}^{- 1}$

$\text{C}{\text{O}}_{2}\left(\text{g}\right) + 2{\text{H}}_{2}\text{O}\left(\text{l}\right) \to \text{C}{\text{H}}_{4}\left(\text{g}\right) + 2{\text{O}}_{2}\left(\text{g}\right); {\text{\Delta}}_{\text{r}}{\text{H}}^{\text{o}} = + 890.3\text{k}\text{J}\text{m}\text{o}{\text{l}}^{- 1}$

Based on the above thermochemical equations, the value of ${\text{\Delta}}_{\text{r}}{\text{H}}^{\text{o}}$ at $\text{298 K}$ for the reaction

$\text{C}\left(\text{g}\text{r}\text{a}\text{p}\text{h}\text{i}\text{t}\text{e}\right) ++2{\text{H}}_{2} \left(\text{g}\right) \to \text{C}{\text{H}}_{4}\left(\text{g}\right)will be:$
questions.solution:
For reaction

${\text{CO}}_{2} {\text{(g)+2H}}_{2} \text{O(l)} \to {\text{CH}}_{4} {\text{(g)+2O}}_{2} \text{(g)}$

${\text{\Delta}}_{\text{r}}{\text{H}}^{\text{o}} = \text{Σ}{\left({\text{\Delta}}_{\text{f}}{\text{H}}^{\text{o}}\right)}_{\text{p}\text{r}\text{o}\text{d}\text{u}\text{c}\text{t}\text{s}} - \text{Σ}{\left({\text{\Delta}}_{\text{f}}{\text{H}}^{\text{o}}\right)}_{\text{r}\text{e}\text{a}\text{c}\text{t}\text{a}\text{n}\text{t}\text{s}}$

$= \left[\left({\text{\Delta}}_{\text{r}}{\text{H}}^{\text{o}}\left(\text{C}{\text{H}}_{4}\right) + 2 \times 0\right) - \left({\text{\Delta}}_{\text{f}}{\text{H}}^{\text{o}}\left(\text{C}{\text{O}}_{2}\right) + 2{\text{\Delta}}_{\text{f}}{\text{H}}^{\text{o}} \left({\text{H}}_{2}\text{O}{}_{}\right)\right)\right]

$+ 890.3 = \left[{\text{\Delta}}_{\text{f}}{\text{H}}^{\text{o}} \left(\text{C}{\text{H}}_{4}\right)\right] - \left[-$393.5 + 2 $\times \left(-$285.8\right)\right]$

${Δ}_{f} H^{o}$ of {\text{CH}}_{4} \text{(g)} = -$74.$8\text{kJ}$/ \text{mol}$

questions.q: The enthalpy of neutralization of ${NH}_{4}OH$ and ${CH}_{3}COOH$is $- 10 . 5kcal{mol}^{- 1}$ and enthalpy of neutralisation of ${NH}_{4}OH$with a strong acid is $- 11 . 7kcal{mol}^{- 1}$. The enthalpy of ionization of ${CH}_{3}COOH$ will be
questions.solution:
Enthalpy of neutralisation is the amount of energy released during the combination of one moe strong monobasic acid neutralised with the one-mole strong monoacidic base.

$H^{+}\left(aq\right) + {OH}^{-}\left(aq\right) \to {H}_{2}O\left(l\right){∆}_{neut .}H = - 13 . 7kcal$

Enthalpy of ionisation of ${CH}_{3}COOH$ & ${NH}_{4}OH$ together

$= - \text{10.5} - \left(- \text{13.7}\right) = + \text{3.2 Kcal}$

Enthalpy of ionisation of only ${NH}_{4}OH$

$= - \text{11.7} - \left(- \text{13.7}\right) = + \text{2 Kcal}$

Enthalpy of ionisation of only ${CH}_{3}COOH$

$= \text{3.2} - \text{2} = 1 . \text{2 Kcal}$

questions.q: A solution of 200 mL of 1 M KOH is added to 200 mL of 1 M HCl and the mixture is well shaken. This rise in temperature ${T}_{1}$ is noted. The experiment is repeated by using 100 mL of each solution and increase in temperature ${T}_{2}$ is again noted. Which of the following is correct?
options: ${T}_{1}$ is four times as large as ${T}_{2}$
questions.solution:
Heat produced by 200 Meq. of KOH + HCl
$= \dfrac{13.7 \times 200}{1000}kcal$
This is used to raise the temperature of 400 mL. Solution say ${T}_{1}$
Thus, $\dfrac{13.7 \times 200}{1000} = 400 \times S \times {T}_{1}$
Now, heat produced by 100 Meq of KOH + HCl
$= \dfrac{13.7 \times 100}{1000}$
Thus, $- \dfrac{13.7 \times 100}{1000} = 200 \times S \times {T}_{2}$
It is evident that ${T}_{1} = {T}_{2}$ .

questions.q:
Calculate the final temperature of the gas, if one mole of an ideal gas is allowed to expand reversibly and adibatically from a temperature of $27 ° C$ and the work done during the process is $\text{3}\text{kJ}$ .
Given \left({C}_{V} \text{=}\text{20}\text{J/K}\right)$
questions.solution:
Given number of moles =1
Initial temperature $= {27}^{o} \text{C} = 300\text{K}$
Work done by the system $= 3\text{kJ} = 3000\text{K}$
It will be $( - )$ because work is done by the system.
Heat capacity at constant volume \left(\text{Cv}\right)\text{=}\text{20}\text{J/k}$
We know that work done
$W = - n{C}_{V} ( {T}_{2} - {T}_{1} )$ ;
$3000 = - 1 \times 20 ( {T}_{2} - 300 )$
$3000 = - 20{T}_{2} + 6000$
$20{T}_{2} = 3000{T}_{2} = \dfrac{3000}{20} = 150\text{K}

questions.q: An ideal gas on isothermal reversible compression from $10 \mathrm{~L}$ to $5 \mathrm{~L}$ performs $1730 \mathrm{~J}$ of work at $300 \mathrm{~K}$. Calculate number of moles of gas involved in compression?  \left(\mathrm{R}=8.314 \mathrm{~J} \mathrm{~K}^{-1} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1}\right)$
questions.solution: \begin{aligned} & $\mathrm{V}}_{1}=10 $\mathrm{~L}, \mathrm{~V}}_{2}=5 $\mathrm{~L}, \mathrm{~W}=$1730 $\mathrm{~J}, \mathrm{~T}=$300 $\mathrm{~K}, \mathrm{R}=$8.314 $\mathrm{JK}^{-1} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1}, \mathrm{n}$\\ & =? \\ & $\mathrm{~W}_{\max }=-$2.303 $\mathrm{nRT} \log _{10} \frac{\mathrm{V}_2}{\mathrm{~V}_1}$\\ & \therefore 1730 $\mathrm{~J}=-$2.303 $\mathrm{n} \times$8.314 $\mathrm{JK}^{-1} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1} \times$300 $\mathrm{~K} \times \log _{10}  \left(\frac{5}{10}\right)$\\ \text{ and } \therefore $\mathrm{n}=\frac{1730 \mathrm{~J}}{-2.303 \times 8.314 \mathrm{JK}^{-1} \mathrm{mo}^{-1} \times 300 \mathrm{~K} \times \log _{10}(0.5)}$\\ \text{ and } \therefore $\mathrm{n}=\frac{1730}{-5744.14 \times(-0.3010)} \mathrm{mol}$\\ \text{ and } \therefore $\mathrm{n}=\frac{1730}{1729} \approx$1 $\mathrm{~mol} \end{aligned}$

questions.q: An adiabatic vessel contains n<sub>1</sub> = 3 mole of diatomic gas. Moment of inertia of each molecule is I = 2.76 x 10<sup>-46</sup> kg m<sup>2</sup> and root-mean-square angular velocity is ${ω}_{0} = 5 \times 1 {0}^{1 2} rad/s$. Another adiabatic vessel contains n<sub>2</sub> = 5 mole of a monatomic gas at a temperature 470 K. Assume gases to be ideal, calculate root-mean-square angular velocity of diatomic molecules when the two vessel are connected by a thin tube of negligible volume. Boltzmann constant k = 1.38 x 10<sup>-23</sup> J/molecule.
questions.solution:
We know according to law of equipartition of energy, each gas molecule has 1/2 kT energy associated with each of its degrees of freedom. As a diatomic gas molecule has two rotational degrees of freedom, final temperature of the system is

${T}_{f ⁡} = \dfrac{{f ⁡}_{1} {n}_{1} {T}_{1} + {f ⁡}_{2} {n}_{2} {T}_{2}}{{f ⁡}_{1} {n}_{1} + {f ⁡}_{2} {n}_{2}}$ ...(i)

Here for diatomic gas,

${f ⁡}_{1} = 5$, n = 3 and T1 = 250 K

For monatomic gas,

${f ⁡}_{2} = 3$, n2 = 5 and T2 = 470 K

Thus from Eq. (i),

${T}_{f ⁡} = \dfrac{5 × 3 × 2 5 0 + 3 × 5 × 4 7 0}{5 × 3 + 3 × 5} = 3 6 0 K$

Thus final mixture of the two gases is at temperature 360 K. If final rms angular velocity of diatomic gas molecules is ${ω}_{rms f ⁡}$,~according to law of equipartition of energy, we have

$\dfrac{1}{2} \text{I} {ω}_{rms f ⁡}^{2} = \text{kT}$

or ${ω}_{rms f ⁡} = \sqrt{\dfrac{2 \text{kT}}{\text{I}}}$

$= \sqrt{\dfrac{2 × \text{1.38} × 1 {0}^{- 2 3} × 3 6 0}{\text{2.76} × 1 {0}^{- 4 6}}}$

${ω}_{rms f ⁡} = 6 × 1 {0}^{1 2} rad/s$
questions.source: 99 Percentile Qs Bank for JEE Main

questions.q: A rigid and insulated tank of& $3m^{3}$ volume is divided into two compartments. One compartment of volume of~$2m^{3}$ contains an ideal gas at~$0 . 8314MPa$ and~$400K$ and while the second compartment of volume~$1m^{3}$ contains the same gas at~$8 . 314MPa$~and $500K$. If the partition between the two compartments is ruptured, the final temperature of the gas is
questions.solution:
Moles of the gas in the first compartment:

${n}_{1} = \dfrac{{P}_{1}{V}_{1}}{\text{RT}1} = \dfrac{\text{0.8314} \times 1{0}^{6} \times 2}{\text{8.314} \times 400} = 500$

Similarly, ${n}_{2} = 2000$

The tank is a rigid and insulated, hence,~$w = 0$ and~$q = 0$.~Therefore,~$\Delta \text{U} = 0$.

Let~${T}_{f}$ and~${P}_{f}$ denote the final temperature and pressure, respectively.

$\Delta \text{U} = {n}_{1}{C}_{V, m}\left[{T}_{f} - {T}_{1}\right] + {n}_{2}{C}_{V, m}\left[{T}_{f} - {T}_{2}\right] = 0$
$500\left({T}_{f} - 400\right) + 2000\left({T}_{f} - 500\right) = 0$
${T}_{f} = \text{480 K}$
